title: ‘सधैँ सधैँ मेरो सपनामा’ कवितामा ध्वनि
nepali: यस लेखमा ध्वनि सिद्घान्तको मूलभूत सिद्धान्तलाई उल्लेख गरी विभिन्न साक्ष्यहरूको आधारमा कवि भूपि शेरचनद्वारा लिखित ‘सधैँ सधैँ मेरो सपनामा’ कविताको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । यस कवितामा जीवन मूल्यको खोजमा नेपालीहरूले भोग्नु परेका युगीन जटिलता, अवमूल्यन र अमानवीयताप्रति ध्वन्यात्मक अर्थ एवम्, व्यङ्ग्यात्मक टिप्पणी कवितामा गरिएको छ । निरङ्कुश शासन र विकृत सामाजिक आर्थिक व्यवस्थाले सताइएका नेपाली जनताको चिररोदनका मझधाराबाट खोसिएका हक, अधिकार स्वतन्त्रता, सुशिक्षा र प्रजातान्त्रिक मूल्यका निम्ति क्रान्तिको आह्वान गरिएको प्रसङ्ग ध्वन्यात्मक रूपमा कवितामा व्यक्त भएको छ । त्यसपछि तत्कालीन शासन व्यवस्थाप्रति तीव्र आक्रोश र विद्रोहको स्वर व्यक्त भएको प्रसङ्ग ध्वन्यात्मक रूपमा अभिव्यञ्जित छ । कवितामा प्रतीकात्मक दृश्य विधान, व्यङ्ग्यात्मक भाव विम्वका कारण कवितामा पूर्वीय काव्यशास्त्रको ध्वनि सौन्दर्भ कलात्मक सफल रूपमा व्यक्त भएको देखिन्छ ।
american_english:
In this article, the fundamental principle of the dhvani theory has been mentioned, and on the basis of various evidences an analysis of the poem "Sadhai Sadhai Mero Sapanama," written by the poet Bhupi Sherchan, has been made.
In this poem, a dhvani-level meaning and a satirical comment have been made in the poem about the epochal complexity, devaluation and inhumanity that Nepalis have had to endure in the search for the values of life.
The episode in which a call for revolution is made for the rights, entitlements, freedom, good education and democratic values snatched away from the midstream of the endless weeping of the Nepali people tormented by despotic rule and a deformed socio-economic order has been expressed in the poem in dhvani form.
After that, the episode in which a voice of intense rage and rebellion against the then ruling order is expressed has been articulated in dhvani form.
Because of the symbolic imagery scheme and the satirical feeling-images in the poem, it is seen that the dhvani dimension of Eastern poetics has been expressed in an artistically successful form in the poem.
british_english:
The present article sets out the underlying principle of the dhvani theory and, on the basis of sundry evidences, offers an analysis of the poem 'Sadhai Sadhai Mero Sapanama', written by the poet Bhupi Sherchan.
In this poem a suggestive meaning and a satirical observation have been made about the epochal intricacy, devaluation and inhumanity which Nepalis have been obliged to undergo in the quest for the values of life.
The passage in which a summons to revolution is issued for the rights, entitlements, liberty, sound education and democratic values torn away from the mid-current of the unending lament of the Nepali people afflicted by despotic rule and a distorted socio-economic dispensation has been voiced suggestively in the poem.
Thereafter, the passage in which a tone of sharp wrath and insurrection against the governing dispensation of the day is voiced has been expressed suggestively.
Owing to the symbolic scheme of imagery and the satirical emotive images in the poem, the dhvani dimension of Eastern poetics is seen to have been conveyed in an artistically accomplished manner in the poem.
australian_english:
This article lays out the basic principle of the dhvani theory and, using a range of evidence, has a good look at the poem 'Sadhai Sadhai Mero Sapanama', written by the poet Bhupi Sherchan.
In this poem there's a suggestive meaning and a satirical dig aimed at the age-old mess, the belittling and the inhumanity Nepalis have had to put up with in their search for the values of life.
The bit where a call goes out for revolution, for the rights, entitlements, freedom, a decent education and democratic values ripped away from the middle of the endless crying of the Nepali people worn down by despotic rule and a bent socio-economic setup, is put across in the poem in dhvani form.
After that, the bit where a loud voice of anger and revolt against the government of the day gets a run is expressed in dhvani form.
Thanks to the symbolic picture-scheme and the satirical feeling-images in the poem, you can see the dhvani side of Eastern poetics coming through in a properly skilful way in the poem.
informal_english:
This piece lays out the basic idea behind dhvani theory and then, off all sorts of evidence, has a look at the poem 'Sadhai Sadhai Mero Sapanama', which the poet Bhupi Sherchan wrote.
In the poem there's a suggestive meaning and a satirical comment about the old-time complications, the belittling and the plain inhumanity our Nepali folk have had to go through while hunting for the values of life.
The part where a call for revolution goes up — for the rights, the entitlements, the freedom, decent schooling and democratic values that got snatched out of the middle of the endless crying of Nepali people hammered by despotic rule and a skew-whiff socio-economic setup — that part comes through in the poem as dhvani.
Then the part where a loud voice of rage and rebellion against the government of the day gets a run comes out as dhvani too.
What with the symbolic picture-scheme and the satirical feeling-images in the poem, you can see the dhvani side of Eastern poetics landing nicely in an artistic way in the poem.
translator_notes: dhvani (the suggestive-meaning theory of Sanskrit poetics) left untransliterated as a technical term; भूपि शेरचन rendered Bhupi Sherchan. Sentence order preserved as in the source.
